narrative.title: Tokenizing the Legacy Command Stream
narrative.scenario: An industrial controller accepts command strings only when they can be split entirely into tokens from its approved vocabulary — spaces are stripped, so the split points are invisible. The parser scans from the current offset, tries every vocabulary word that matches a prefix there, and recurses on the rest; the command is accepted when some chain of matches consumes the whole string.
narrative.inputFormat: A string s and an array wordDict of vocabulary words.
narrative.outputFormat: true when s can be segmented entirely into dictionary words, false otherwise.
constraints: s and wordDict[i] consist of lowercase letters

complexity.optimalTime: O(n^2) with memoization over offsets (bare source recursion is exponential)

testCases.explanation: "leet" consumes the first four letters and "code" the rest.
Both parsings — "cats and" and "cat sand" — strand the trailing "og".

hintLevels: Level 1: The question at each offset is binary — can the rest of the stream be tokenized from here?
Level 2: Loop every end position past the offset; if that slice sits in the dictionary and the remainder parses, the answer is yes.
Level 3: Different match orders re-derive the same offsets constantly — memoize failing offsets to collapse the exponential blow-up on adversarial inputs.
